nominees.name: Eric A. Swanson
nominees.affiliation: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (Research Laboratory of Electronics), USA

motivation: In 1991 Fujimoto, Huang and Swanson showed that low-coherence interferometry with broadband light can produce cross-sectional images of living tissue with micrometre resolution. They turned the short coherence length of ultrafast and broadband sources into a new way of seeing: time-of-flight echoes of light used to look non-invasively inside the eye, the arteries and other organs. Later advances in Fourier-domain and swept-source detection, many from the same community, made OCT fast and sensitive, and it is now performed tens of millions of times a year. It has changed how blindness-causing diseases such as macular degeneration and glaucoma are diagnosed and treated. OCT is a clear example of curiosity-driven optical physics, including coherence, interferometry and ultrashort-pulse technology, becoming a tool of enormous benefit to humanity. It shows how precise measurement of light can make visible what no one could see before, and it opened the field of optical biomedical imaging.
